doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Piano duos, Mingus and the seventies
title: Chick Corea, 'Duende', Circle and Weather Report
summary: He recounts playing with Chick Corea and an audition for Circle.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: I haven’t had the pleasure of playing with Herbie Hancock yet. I would like to do that once.
So would I.
The only time I really played with Chick Corea was in the Scientology connection at different places.
Didn’t he write that one tune for you?
I was going to say. We did it at his studio as a duo and then he wrote strings and over dubbed string parts.
“Duende” right?

“Duende” yeah. One time I was invited up to someone’s apartment with Chick, Dave Holland, Barry Altschul, and Anthony Braxton. I think Anthony and I were auditioning to play with the group called “Circle” and Anthony won out.
Really?

Yeah. Later on when he wrote that “Duende” I went to his place and we played together. He, whatever the process is called, copied my sound; duplicating my sound on his keyboard. I forget what that’s all called.
Sampling.
Sampling. That’s what it’s called. We played a little bit and I think he had a mind to try me out for his group then that the saxophone player, [the] other saxophone player, finally did very well.
Steve Wilson?
No . . . not Ernie.
Eric Marienthal.
Eric Marienthal, yeah. He was the right guy obviously.
For the Electric Band?
Yeah.
I can’t imagine you in that band for all the world. That was almost like a fusion band.
He couldn’t either.
[Laughing] That would’ve been a mismatch of historic proportions I think.
I was curious with Weather Report. I wondered if I could find some niche in that kind of situation but it never occurred.
